name: Apply ESOI to a project
description: Gives anyone a way to turn what a project is for into specifications that stay true as the project changes, without first building tooling or learning a new vocabulary.
purpose: Turn a project's intent into specifications that are checked, measured and selected by metric, so the structure keeps evolving with the intent.
approach: Start from plain documents and templates that anyone can fill in by hand, then add checks, measurement and selection so the records stay true to the intent.
out_of_scope: Deciding what a project is for: that is the project's own top intent.
milestones: 1. Adoption effort: one recorded newcomer trial applying ESOI from the documents only, and one with the tools.
knowledge: The author's skill: its definitions, the intent specification, the five specification templates and the principles; the adopters' experience.
measures_of_success: A newcomer applies ESOI from the documents alone with few questions, and a project's records pass the structure check. Standing conditions: A person or an agent can specify an intent, compare the alternatives of each solution by metric and let the best one be used, with every part reachable from the specifications.
parameters: The project's own top intent, and which implementations of the building blocks to use.
inputs: A project's intent, in its owner's words.
outputs: Specifications for the project (an intent folder with its five record types), checks and metric results.
effects: None beyond the files the project keeps.
usage_notes: Start from the documents and templates; add the Python tools where checks, measurement and selection should run by themselves.

name: Intent registry
description: Keeps a project's whole intent as one set of linked records that a person and a program read the same way, so the reasons behind the code never live only in someone's head.
purpose: Record every problem, solution, implementation, ideal and metric of a repository as linked records that people and checks both read.
approach: Store each intent item as one record with fixed fields and links that resolve in both directions.
out_of_scope: Holding measured results, and prose design documents.
milestones: 1. Record completeness: every record has every template field filled and every link resolving both ways, and all record cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: The intent template in the evolvable-structure skill; Joshua's Project Documentation board (solution definitions apart from implementations); requirements traceability practice.
measures_of_success: A reader can follow any file to its problem and ideal, and every record is complete. Standing conditions: Every intent item is one record with every template field filled; every link resolves both ways; every file reaches a solution through the ownership map.
parameters: The template's fields per type.
inputs: Hand-edited records of each type, the ownership map.
outputs: A linked intent network that the check, the tracker and the selection read.
effects: None.
usage_notes: Add or edit a record before building a new capability; the check names anything missing.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Template sync
description: Makes the author's own template wording the only definition of a record's fields, so the registry cannot drift from it or grow fields of its own.
purpose: Derive the registry's fields from the intent template in the skill so the author's wording stays the single definition.
approach: Read the fields from the template itself and report each field a record leaves unfilled after the template changes.
out_of_scope: Interpreting or extending the template.
milestones: 1. Template agreement: the registry's fields equal the template's fields and no required field is left empty after a refinement, and all template cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: The skill's `SKILL.md` as the source of truth; derived-copy practice already used for the standing instructions.
measures_of_success: A template refinement shows up as named missing fields on the next check, with no hand edit of any schema. Standing conditions: The registry's fields equal the template's fields after every refinement.
parameters: Path to the skill.
inputs: The skill's intent template.
outputs: A committed field list per type.
effects: Fails the check when the committed field list is stale.
usage_notes: Run after Joshua edits the template; public CI, which cannot read the skill, checks records against the committed list.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Ownership map
description: Shows that every file exists for a reason by tracing it to the problem and ideal it serves, so code that serves nothing is found and removed.
purpose: Assign every file to exactly one component and every component to the solutions it serves, so code with no purpose cannot hide.
approach: Give each file one owner and trace that owner through its solutions to a problem and an ideal.
out_of_scope: Describing what the code does.
milestones: 1. Trace completeness: every file reaches a problem and an ideal through a component and a solution, and all ownership cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Layered and hexagonal architecture; code owners practice; the repository's split rule.
measures_of_success: Code that serves no solution is found and removed. Standing conditions: No file unowned, no component serving nothing, no module past the size ceiling, imports pointing inward.
parameters: Layer order, size ceiling.
inputs: The file tree and the component records.
outputs: File-to-solution links and the generated component index.
effects: None.
usage_notes: A new file joins a component in the same change; a file that fits no solution is a sign the code should go.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Implementation selection
description: Lets a project switch between alternatives by changing data, and fails loudly on a mistyped name instead of quietly running something else.
purpose: Choose which implementation serves a swappable solution by name, configuration or table default.
approach: Resolve the implementation from a name, a configuration value or a recorded default, and refuse an unknown name by listing the valid choices.
out_of_scope: Deciding which implementation is best, and branching on the choice at every call.
milestones: 1. Resolution correctness: a recorded run of the entry-point rival and of the chosen implementation on the selection cases.
knowledge: Ports and adapters; plugin registries; lazy loading of optional dependencies.
measures_of_success: Every switch works from configuration alone and no typo falls back silently. Standing conditions: Switching is a data change; an unknown name fails with the choices; every listed implementation loads.
parameters: Solution id, implementation name, configuration overrides.
inputs: The implementations declared in code and the records.
outputs: The chosen implementation's class and its configuration type.
effects: Imports the chosen implementation lazily.
usage_notes: Every swappable solution has declared implementations and a selected cell whose value equals the measured winner or a declared tie.

name: Measurement harness
description: Makes every result trustworthy by running the code that ships against the solution's cases and recording where the result came from, so anyone can rerun it.
purpose: Run each implementation of a solution against that solution's cases through the live code and record the result with its provenance.
approach: Drive the shipped implementation over fixed cases and record each score with its commit, case hash, cost and tokens under a call budget.
out_of_scope: Ranking implementations, and tests that only check that code runs.
milestones: 1. Provenance completeness: every latest result has a clean commit, a case hash, cost and tokens, run through shipped code, and all provenance cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Evaluation practice for language models (held-out cases, staged sample sizes, judged rubrics); experiment tracking; the eval ladder of three, ten and thirty cases.
measures_of_success: Any result can be rerun from its record, and no result was produced by code other than what ships. Standing conditions: Every eval solution has cases, a scorer and implementations that drive shipped code; every recorded result carries its commit, case hash, cost and tokens; a call budget stops a run.
parameters: Solution, implementation, case subset, call budget.
inputs: Case files, the implementation, any live services the cases need.
outputs: A results row per run.
effects: Model spend on live runs; refuses to run against production.
usage_notes: Start live runs small and stop at the budget; re-record on committed code after any change to measured code or cases.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Leaderboard
description: Turns recorded results into an honest verdict on which implementation is best, and says so plainly when the result is a tie or the evidence is not comparable.
purpose: Decide from recorded results which implementation of a solution is best, or whether they tie.
approach: Compare the recorded scores of the implementations on the same cases and call a winner only when the gap is beyond the noise.
out_of_scope: Running implementations, and comparing results from different case sets.
milestones: 1. Ranking correctness: the verdict matches the known right verdict on every pinned result set, ties and different case sets included. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Statistical noise in small judged samples; cost and token accounting; Pareto comparison of quality and cost.
measures_of_success: Its verdicts match known rankings on pinned cases and never call a tie a win. Standing conditions: A win is called only outside the noise margin; ties, losses and unmeasured arms are labelled as such; comparison-only arms are never rivals.
parameters: Noise margin and spend tolerance per component.
inputs: The results log.
outputs: A verdict per solution and a ranked board.
effects: None.
usage_notes: The check requires the selected implementation to be the winner or a declared tie with a reason.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Discriminating cases
description: Shows that a solution's cases can actually fail, which is the only evidence a measure has when the solution has no rival to compare against.
purpose: Prove that a solution's cases can tell a sound implementation from a naive one, even when only one implementation exists.
approach: Write deliberately naive baselines and show that each one fails the cases.
out_of_scope: Inventing rivals that exist only to lose a comparison.
milestones: 1. Case discrimination: a recorded run of the share of solutions whose naive baselines all fail their cases.
knowledge: Mutation testing; the gap between a passing test and a meaningful one.
measures_of_success: No case set passes everything that is put in front of it. Standing conditions: Every invariant solution has at least one naive baseline that fails its cases.
parameters: None.
inputs: A solution's cases and its naive baselines.
outputs: A pass or fail per baseline.
effects: None.
usage_notes: Write the naive version a first draft would produce, not a deliberately silly one.

name: Rule engine
description: Runs any set of rules on every change quickly enough that nobody skips it, and keeps rule exceptions honest by reporting those that no longer apply.
purpose: Apply a set of rules to a repository on each change and report every violation by rule and path.
approach: Run every enabled rule against the tree, report violations by rule id and path, and flag any accepted exception that no longer applies.
out_of_scope: Deciding which rules exist, and judging code quality beyond the rules given.
milestones: 1. Check dependability: a clean tree is never flagged and an exception that no longer applies is always reported, and all mutation cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Architecture tests and linters (import-linter, ArchUnit); plugin systems; the leaderboard (reused, not copied).
measures_of_success: A clean tree is never flagged, an exception that no longer applies is reported, and the run is fast enough that nobody skips it. Standing conditions: Any rule written to the rule interface runs and reports by rule and path; a repository can disable a rule or add one by configuration; a clean tree passes; strict mode refuses results from uncommitted code; an exception lives only as a waiver with a reason, and is reported when it stops applying.
parameters: Strict mode; the rule ids to disable; the plugins to load.
inputs: The repository, the registry, the results log, the waivers, the configuration.
outputs: A list of violations, each led by its rule id, and an exit code.
effects: Blocks a commit or a test run that breaks a rule.
usage_notes: Keep the engine free of any one rule: a new rule is a rule group written to the interface, never an edit to the runner. Which rules exist is the business of structure-rules.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Structure rules
description: Keeps the rule set honest: each rule exists because of a mistake that really happened, and is dropped when it stops catching anything.
purpose: Decide which structural rules a repository is held to, each with the mistake that justifies it and the evidence that it still catches something.
approach: Admit a rule only with the mistake it prevents and evidence that it still catches something, and remove it when it stops.
out_of_scope: Rules that no one can fix.
milestones: 1. Violation detection: every injected violation is reported by the right rule and path. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: The repository's numbered rules (esoi rules); architecture tests; Principle 12 (minimalism).
measures_of_success: Every injected violation is reported by the right rule and path, and every rule has caught something real. Standing conditions: Each rule catches a mistake that has happened and names its rule and path; a rule that stops catching anything is removed; a limit such as the module size is a setting of the rule, not part of it.
parameters: Per-rule settings: the module size ceiling, the layers, the rule ids disabled.
inputs: The repository, the registry, the results log.
outputs: One problem line per violation, led by the rule id.
effects: None itself; the engine blocks a commit on its output.
usage_notes: Add a rule when a mistake has happened twice; delete a rule that stops catching anything. The statement of a rule is listed by esoi rules; the mistake behind it is not yet recorded per rule.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Review tracker
description: Lets a reviewer see the whole intent network and its latest results in one place and make decisions there, without learning the repository layout.
purpose: Put the whole intent network and its current results in front of a human reviewer, and carry their edits back.
approach: Build one review view from the records and results, and return the reviewer's edits to the records so that rebuilds keep them.
out_of_scope: Holding any truth beyond the review columns.
milestones: 1. Review coverage: every record and verdict is present in the sheet and every reviewer edit survives a rebuild and reaches the repository, and all tracker cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Spreadsheets as the team's review medium; two-way sync keyed by record id.
measures_of_success: Joshua can make and record every review decision from the sheet. Standing conditions: Every record and its latest verdict appears in one sheet; reviewer edits survive rebuilds and flow back to the repository.
parameters: Which tabs, which columns a reviewer may edit.
inputs: The registry and the results log.
outputs: Generated tracker tables and the synced sheet.
effects: Writes the sheet.
usage_notes: Rebuild after any registry or result change; the check fails when the tracker is stale.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Consumer check
description: Lets a system built on the library prove it uses the library's solutions correctly, without copying the library's checks or exposing its own data.
purpose: Let a system built on a library record which library solution each of its parts serves, score its own implementations with the library's cases, and see its version lag.
approach: Map each integration point to a library solution, score the consumer's stores with the library's cases, and report how far its pinned version trails.
out_of_scope: Copying the library's checks into the consumer, and putting the consumer's private data in the library.
milestones: 1. Consumer soundness: no unmapped integration point, no consumer store unscored by the library's cases, and the pin lag visible, and all consumer cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Consumer-driven contract testing; the library's own structure check and cases.
measures_of_success: The consumer passes with nothing unmapped, unscored or unexplained. Standing conditions: Every integration point maps to a library solution; every consumer store is scored by the library's cases; the pin's lag is visible.
parameters: The consumer's registry, root, requirements, solutions and results files; whether lag fails.
inputs: The consumer repository.
outputs: Violations and notes.
effects: None.
usage_notes: Run in the consumer's tests; bump the pin after the library's changes land.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: The standard
description: Gives a newcomer one document that shows end to end how a solution is shaped and how to adopt that shape in another repository.
purpose: Teach anyone, person or AI, how a solution is shaped in this structure and how another repository adopts it.
approach: Lay out the shape of a solution and the steps to adopt it in one document that can be followed alone.
out_of_scope: Repeating what automated checks already enforce.
milestones: 1. Adoption effort: one recorded newcomer trial of following only the standard in a fresh repository.
knowledge: the adopting repositories as worked examples; the evolvable-structure skill.
measures_of_success: Someone following it alone reaches a passing check. Standing conditions: One document gives the shape of a solution end to end and the steps to adopt it elsewhere.
parameters: None.
inputs: The registry's rules and examples.
outputs: The standard document.
effects: None.
usage_notes: Read first; update in the same change as any rule.

name: Structure budget
description: Keeps the structure from turning into overhead by weighing what it costs each change against what it catches.
purpose: Keep the structure's own cost in view and prune what stops paying.
approach: Weigh the effort the structure adds to each change against the real mistakes it catches, and remove what catches nothing.
out_of_scope: Removing rules that still catch real mistakes.
milestones: 1. Structure cost against catches: the time the check adds and the real violations it caught, recorded over a month.
knowledge: Principle 12 (minimalism) and the skill's difficulties; developer-experience research.
measures_of_success: Small changes stay small and every rule has caught something real. Standing conditions: The effort the structure adds to a change is known, and rules, records and checks that catch nothing are removed.
parameters: None yet.
inputs: The check's history, time per check, files touched per change.
outputs: A periodic report of cost against catches.
effects: Proposes removals.
usage_notes: Not built yet; this record holds the place so the cost is not forgotten.

name: When metrics are run
description: Ensures decisions rest on current evidence and that spending on measurement is approved and proportionate, by settling in advance when each metric runs.
purpose: Decide when each metric is run, in what stages, with what limit, who approves the spend, and when its result stops counting.
approach: Set a trigger, stages, a call budget, an approver and a staleness rule for each metric, running free metrics on every change and paid ones only for a decision.
out_of_scope: Deciding how a metric is implemented or which alternative is best.
milestones: 1. Decisions backed by current results: every staleness case passes, so a stale or missing result is reported and a current one is not. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Evaluation practice for models (staged and stratified samples, call budgets, noise); continuous integration practice; the cost of re-running against the cost of deciding wrongly.
measures_of_success: Decisions are backed by current results, spend is approved and proportionate, and stale results are found at the change rather than at a release. Standing conditions: Offline metrics run on every change; paid metrics run only when a decision depends on them, in staged samples; every recorded result can be told current from stale.
parameters: Trigger: every change for the offline metrics, in the test suite and in continuous integration; a paid metric only when a decision depends on it, in staged samples inside a call budget and with Joshua's approval.
inputs: The committed code, the case files and the results log.
outputs: A row per run in the results log with the commit and the hash of the cases; the strict check's verdict.
effects: Offline metrics call no paid service and no network; a paid metric calls a model only when it is run on a decision. Re-recording changes only the results log.
usage_notes: After changing measured code or cases, commit, then run `esoi run --stale`, then commit the results.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Skill distribution
description: Lets an author keep a skill in a private place and publish a complete, clean public copy that cannot go stale or leak.
purpose: Publish an author's skill from the private folder where it is maintained as a complete public folder that people install without anything else.
approach: Generate the public copy from the source, check it against the source, and scan it for private terms, paths and addresses.
out_of_scope: Deciding what the skill says, and hosting the published copy.
milestones: 1. Skill copy agreement: each public copy equals what the source generates and every planted leak is caught, and all skill cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: The skill's own layout (one authoritative file and supporting notes); plugin and skill folder conventions of the agents that read them; derived-copy practice used for the intent template.
measures_of_success: After any edit of the source, a check names exactly what is stale; a planted private term, path or email is always caught; a fresh install equals the published copy. Standing conditions: The public copy always equals what the source generates, nothing private is in it, and installing it is one step in each of three ways.
parameters: The source folder, the include list, the substitutions, the list of private terms.
inputs: The author's skill folder and a list of private terms that is never published.
outputs: A public skill folder, a plugin manifest and marketplace file, and an installed copy.
effects: Writes the public folders; fails the check on a stale copy or a leak; an install writes into a skills folder.
usage_notes: Run the sync after the source changes and commit the result; run the check in a place that can see the source and the private terms; people install with the plugin, a download or the command.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: ESOI applied to AI behaviour
description: Makes an AI agent apply the principles in its own work, and shows by measurement which way of giving it the principles works.
purpose: Make an AI agent act by the evolvable-structure principles when designing, building, writing and advising.
approach: Give the agent the principles in a chosen form and measure, case by case, whether its replies act on them compared with the same agent without them.
out_of_scope: Judging an agent's general ability, and deciding what the principles say.
milestones: 1. Behaviour adherence: a recorded run of each arm that calls a model, on the staged sample.
knowledge: The author's skill and its principles, especially principle 4 (humans need only review metrics, not implementations, though they can still add value to implementations) and principle 7 (perspectives are implementations); evaluation practice for language models (cases with an expected behaviour and a failure mode, staged samples, a no-instructions baseline); practice for loading skills and standing instructions.
measures_of_success: The share of cases where the agent's reply acts by the principle, per principle, compared with the same agent without the instructions, with restraint and kept-qualifier cases counted as often as build cases. Standing conditions: Cases cover every principle, including cases where the right behaviour is to hold back or to keep a qualifier; each way of giving the agent the principles is measured on the same cases; the instructions in use are the measured winner or a declared tie; the closing summary of every use says how the principles were applied.
parameters: The model, the way the principles are given (standing instructions, on request, none), the case subset and a call budget.
inputs: A task prompt an agent might be sent.
outputs: The agent's reply and, for a judged run, a verdict with a reason.
effects: A live measurement calls a model and costs money; nothing else.
usage_notes: Run the offline checks on every change; run a live arm only when a decision depends on it and the spend is approved (esoi/metric-run-policy.md). A person who corrects an agent's behaviour adds or edits a case, not only the instructions, so the correction is measured from then on.

name: The ESOI steps
description: Gives a person or an agent a stated order for applying ESOI, so the work neither stalls on what comes next nor skips the steps that matter.
purpose: Give the order in which to define and apply ESOI to anything new or changed, and say where to loop back when something changes.
approach: State the steps in order from why to what to how, mark the human steps, and name where to return when something changes.
out_of_scope: Restating what each record type asks, and prescribing tools.
milestones: 1. Steps followed: one recorded trial by a newcomer and one by an agent following the steps on real work.
knowledge: The 2020 Project Documentation board checklist; the author's skill (definitions, intent template, principles); trials of people and agents applying the steps.
measures_of_success: Trials complete the steps without asking what comes next, with no silent skips, and end with a passing check and a checked metric. Standing conditions: Every principle is carried out by at least one step; human steps are marked; metrics and their checks come before implementations; the process names how it is itself improved.
parameters: The size of the work (a sentence per step for a small change, full records for a project) and the next milestone that sets how much structure pays for itself.
inputs: An intent stated by a person.
outputs: Linked records, a checked metric, measured implementations and a recorded selection; a short summary of how the steps were applied.
effects: None beyond the records written.
usage_notes: Read skill/evolvable-structure/steps.md; the one-hour guide is a short first pass through it. Record a trial whenever someone follows the steps, and change the steps when a trial shows a confusing, skipped or missing step.

name: Documentation and templates
description: Lets anyone start applying ESOI by hand with only documents, before any tool is installed.
purpose: Explain ESOI and give fill-in templates that need no code so anyone can apply it by hand first.
approach: Explain each idea in plain words and provide templates that can be filled in without code.
out_of_scope: Restating the author's template in other words.
milestones: 1. Newcomer effort: one recorded run of a newcomer following the guides in a fresh repository.
knowledge: The skill's definitions, principles and intent template, quoted.
measures_of_success: Someone following the guides alone reaches a passing check. Standing conditions: A newcomer can write an overall network and a first solution from the templates alone.
parameters: None.
inputs: The skill's SKILL.md.
outputs: Explanations, guides and generated templates.
effects: None.
usage_notes: Read the explanation first, then copy a template.

name: Follow the steps
description: Puts the written order of steps where people already look: in the public skill and in the guides.
purpose: Give the written order in which to define and apply ESOI, as shipped in the public skill and the guides.
approach: Ship the steps with every copy of the skill and point the guides to them.
out_of_scope: Tooling for applying the steps, and restating the intent template.
milestones: 1. Steps trial: one recorded trial by a newcomer and one by an agent following the steps on a real piece of work.
knowledge: The 2020 Project Documentation board checklist; the author's skill.
measures_of_success: Trials complete the steps without asking what comes next and with no silent skips. Standing conditions: The steps file ships in every copy of the skill, the guides point to it, and each trial of following it is recorded.
parameters: None.
inputs: The skill's steps.md.
outputs: The steps in the public skill and the guides that point to them.
effects: None.
usage_notes: Edit steps.md in the author's skill and run `esoi skill sync`; never edit the copy here.

name: Local ESOI index
description: Answers where to look for a project from the person's own index, so it works for projects no guidance ever named.
purpose: Find which projects ESOI is applied to, how they relate and where to look first in each.
approach: Look the project up in the person's own index of pointers and relations, and answer none for a path outside every project.
out_of_scope: Holding anything about a project beyond a pointer and its relations.
milestones: 1. Local index lookup: the live lookup passes every lookup case, including projects the guidance never named and paths outside every project. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: How the folder for a tool's user settings works in other tools; the principle of finding and reusing structure instead of rebuilding it.
measures_of_success: The lookup cases pass for projects the guidance never named, and a lookup that routes from frozen rows or from a project's records alone fails them. Standing conditions: A question about where to look is answered for any listed project, including one added later, and for a path outside every project the answer is none.
parameters: Where the index folder is (an environment variable, else a folder in the user's home).
inputs: A path, a project id or a request to list.
outputs: The project containing the path with its first file to read and its specifications, the ids related in a given way, or the listed ids.
effects: Writes only the index folder; makes no network call.
usage_notes: The skill's index says to read the person's local index first; the commands `esoi projects init`, `add`, `check`, `index` and `where` keep it.
verdict_detail: passes more cases than records_only; passes more cases than skill_rows

name: ESOI behaviour judge
description: Grades the replies a pattern match cannot grade and shows how far its grading agrees with people, so a lenient judge is caught.
purpose: Grade whether one reply acts by the principles when a pattern match cannot tell, and show how far the grading agrees with people.
approach: Grade each reply against a rubric and score the grader against labelled replies, counting false passes and false fails apart.
out_of_scope: Grading general quality, and being the behaviour measure itself.
milestones: 1. Judge agreement: a person's label on a sample of recorded replies, and the judge's agreement with those labels recorded.
knowledge: Practice for model judges (agreement with human labels, preference for its own phrasing, position and length bias); the author's verdicts as the authority on what counts as acting by the principles; the case rubric of expected behaviour and failure mode.
measures_of_success: Agreement with human verdicts on held-out replies, with the two kinds of error visible, and a judge that passes everything is caught. Standing conditions: Every judge is scored by its agreement with labelled replies, with false passes and false fails counted apart; the labels move from the case author's to a person's; the judge is measured again when the model behind it changes.
parameters: The judge model, the rubric and the labelled replies.
inputs: A behaviour case and one reply.
outputs: A verdict (pass or fail) and a one-line reason.
effects: A model call per reply, which costs money.
usage_notes: A sub-solution of esoi-for-ai, kept separate because its best is agreement with a human verdict, not acting by the principles (docs/explanation/esoi-for-ai.md). A behaviour score graded by a judge no person has checked is reported as such.

name: Behave by ESOI
description: Shows with cases, not opinion, whether an agent acts by the principles and which way of giving them works best, restraint included.
purpose: Measure case by case whether an AI agent's reply acts by the evolvable-structure principles.
approach: Run the same cases through each way of giving the agent the principles and classify each reply against the principle the case tests.
out_of_scope: Judging the quality of work in general, and rewording the principles.
milestones: 1. ESOI behaviour cases: a recorded run of each arm on the staged sample.
knowledge: The author's skill, its principles and its nuance rules; the intent template; evaluation practice for language models (cases with an expected behaviour and a failure mode, a no-instructions baseline, staged samples).
measures_of_success: Offline: the recorded replies are classified as their authors meant and a keyword-stuffing baseline fails the restraint cases. Live: the skill arms pass more cases than no skill, with restraint cases passing as often as build cases. Standing conditions: Every principle has cases, including cases of holding back and of keeping a qualifier; the recorded good replies pass and the recorded bad replies fail; every arm that calls a model is measured on the same cases and sample.
parameters: The arm (standing instructions, on request, no skill), the model and judge model, the case subset (--sample, --only) and the call budget (--max-calls).
inputs: The rows of cases.csv, the bundled skill, and for a live arm a model command in ESOI_MODEL_COMMAND.
outputs: A reply per case, a pass or fail with a note, and a headline of passes per principle.
